the best scenario is to have two aerated tanks with a total volume of 1365m3.
the installation of a buffer tank upstream, followed by an aeration basin and a clarifier, is a good option to reduce the impact of organic pollution peaks.

the installation of a buffer basin before the activated sludge biological stage, and the installation of a first clarifier before the second aerated basin, are the most suitable options to improve the performance of an activated sludge WWPT in terms of COD removal, during grape harvest periods, and to avoid sludge bulking.

the following objectives : (1) To study the impact of different scenarios on the WWTP performances in terms of COD, BOD5 and nitrogen removals.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the installation of an aerated stage followed by a first clarification, then by another aerated stage and a second clarifying, seems to be the best solution to face the high organic flows due during the grape harvest periods.
the best scenario for the studied WWTP is the one with two aerated basing followed by two clarifiers.

the best solution for the WWTP is to install a buffer basin upstream of the existing biological basins, and then to install a second aerated basin, with the same volume as the first one, followed by a clarifier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the installation of a third basin of 1364 m3, in parallel, and with a buffer basin of 1360 m3, upstream of the existing treatment line, would allow to achieve the same treatment efficiency as that of the current treatment line, but with a better reduction of the COD.
the WWTP efficiency is improved by installing an intermediate basin and by adding a second clarifier to the process line.
the best solution for the studied WWTP would be to install an aerated basin of 136.5 m3 followed by a clarifier of the same size.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a single basin of the volume 1365 m ^{3}, with a hydraulic retention time (HRT) of 12 h, can be used to face high organic loads, as encountered during grape harvest periods, and to achieve the same reduction of COD, as obtained in the actual treatment line.

, to cope with the high organic loads during grape harvesting period, it is better to install an aerated basin of 1360 m3 followed by a clarifier of 400 m3, and then a second aerated basin of the same volume and a second clarifiers.
the installation of a third clarifier is not necessary to improve the treatment of the WWTP.
